subtopics.name: History Features and Applications of C
Role of C in System Programming

questions.title: ATM Receipt Header Builder
questions.description:
An ATM prints a receipt header containing a customer name bracketed by lines of equals signs. Read the customer name from a single line and print the header.

Input Format:
A single line containing the customer NAME (may contain spaces).

Output Format:
Print exactly four lines:
"========================"
"ATM RECEIPT"
"Customer: <NAME>"
"========================"

Constraints:
1 <= length(NAME) <= 80

questions.title: ATM Withdrawal Approval
questions.description:
An ATM checks whether a customer's requested withdrawal amount does not exceed the available balance. Read the balance and the requested amount and print "Approved" or "Declined".

Input Format:
Two space-separated floating-point values: BALANCE and AMOUNT.

Output Format:
Print "Approved" if AMOUNT <= BALANCE, otherwise "Declined".

Constraints:
0.0 <= BALANCE <= 1000000.0, 0.0 <= AMOUNT <= 1000000.0

questions.title: ATM Withdrawal Validator
questions.description:
An ATM dispenses cash only if the requested amount is positive and does not exceed the account balance. Read balance and amount. If amount <= 0 print INVALID_AMOUNT. Else if amount > balance print INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS. Otherwise print OK new_balance where new_balance = balance - amount.

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers: balance and amount.

Output Format:
A single line: INVALID_AMOUNT, INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS, or OK new_balance.

Constraints:
0 <= balance <= 100000, -1000 <= amount <= 100000

questions.title: Absolute Value Function
questions.description:
Read an integer and print its absolute value by calling a function named abs_val that returns the absolute value of its int parameter.

Input Format:
A single integer N.

Output Format:
Print the absolute value of N.

Constraints:
-1000000 <= N <= 1000000

questions.title: Absolute Value via ABS Macro
questions.description:
A math library defines a macro ABS(x) that returns the absolute value. Read an integer n, then print ABS(n).

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n.

Output Format:
The absolute value of n.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= n <= 10^9

questions.title: Access Student Record Fields
questions.description:
Define a struct Student with members id and age. Read the id and age, then print them in the format "ID=<id> Age=<age>".

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers id and age.

Output Format:
The string "ID=<id> Age=<age>".

Constraints:
1 <= id <= 10^9, 1 <= age <= 150

questions.title: Active Array Sum via Pointer to Pointer
questions.description:
A traffic monitor keeps two parallel arrays A and B (each of n integers). A flag f selects which array is active. Use a pointer-to-pointer to the active array's first element pointer to compute and print the sum of the active array.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n integers for array A.
Line 3: n integers for array B.
Line 4: integer flag f (0 selects A, 1 selects B).

Output Format:
The sum of the active array.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -10^4 <= value <= 10^4, f in {0, 1}

questions.title: Active Setting via Pointer to Pointer
questions.description:
A configuration manager has two settings (a and b). Given a flag f (0 means use a, 1 means use b), set an active pointer to the chosen setting and use a pointer-to-pointer to print the active setting's value.

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated integers: a b f.

Output Format:
The value of the active setting.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= a, b <= 10^9, f in {0, 1}

questions.title: Add Two Numbers via Function
questions.description:
Read two integers and print their sum by calling a function named add that takes two int parameters and returns their sum.

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers A and B.

Output Format:
Print A + B as an integer.

Constraints:
-1000000 <= A, B <= 1000000

questions.title: Alarm Flag Set Operation
questions.description:
An alarm subsystem uses bit positions in a 32-bit register to denote which alarms are armed. Read the current register r and an alarm index k. Print the new register value after arming alarm k (setting bit k to 1).

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers: register value r and alarm index k.

Output Format:
A single integer: r with bit k set.

Constraints:
0 <= r <= 4294967295, 0 <= k <= 31

questions.title: Alpha Check via ctype Include
questions.description:
A program includes both <stdio.h> and <ctype.h>. Read a single character, then print 'Y' if it is alphabetic, 'N' otherwise.

Input Format:
A single line containing one character (may be preceded by whitespace).

Output Format:
A single character 'Y' or 'N' on its own line.

Constraints:
The input is a single ASCII character.
questions.inputconstrains: Input is a single ASCII character

questions.title: Anagram Group Counter
questions.description:
A linguist receives a list of n lowercase words (no spaces, length 1 to 100). Two words are anagrams if they share the same multiset of letters. Count the number of distinct anagram classes (each word belongs to exactly one class).

Input Format:
Line 1: an integer n.
Next n lines: one lowercase word per line.

Output Format:
A single integer — the number of distinct anagram classes.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= word length <= 100
questions.input2:
6
abc
bca
cab
abd
dba
bad

questions.title: Anagram Pair Check Drill
questions.description:
Given two lowercase words of equal length, determine whether they are anagrams (contain the same multiset of letters).

Input Format:
Two lines, each containing one lowercase word.

Output Format:
Print "Yes" if they are anagrams, otherwise print "No".

Constraints:
1 <= length of each word <= 1000
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of each word <= 1000, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Anti-Diagonal Sum Calculator
questions.description:
An image processing tool computes the sum of the anti-diagonal (top-right to bottom-left) of an N x N matrix. Print the sum. Do not use qsort.

Input Format:
First line: integer N. Next N lines: N space-separated integers.

Output Format:
A single integer: the anti-diagonal sum.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, -1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Append-only Audit Trail Builder
questions.description:
An audit service records N event identifiers (integers) to /tmp/atom_day20_audit.txt with the prefix EVT: per line. First open the file in write mode and write a single header line containing just # (to truncate any prior content), then close. Then reopen in append mode and append EVT:<id> for each event, then close. Finally reopen in read mode, scan the file byte-by-byte with fgetc (no fscanf/fgets/fread), and count how many EVT: lines exist, then close and print EVENTS <k>.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N. Line 2: N space-separated integers.

Output Format:
A single line: EVENTS <k>.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -10000 <= id <= 10000

questions.title: Armstrong Number Range Finder
questions.description:
An Armstrong number is an integer that equals the sum of its own digits each raised to the power of the number of digits (e.g. 153 = 1^3 + 5^3 + 3^3). Read a closed range [LOW, HIGH] and print every Armstrong number in that range, each on its own line. Use nested loops and a manual power computation (no math library).

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers LOW and HIGH.

Output Format:
Print every Armstrong number in [LOW, HIGH] on its own line, in ascending order.

Constraints:
0 <= LOW <= HIGH <= 100000

questions.title: Array Echo Space Separated Drill
questions.description:
Read an integer N followed by N integers, store them in an array, and print them back on one line space-separated.

Input Format:
First line: integer N. Second line: N space-separated integers.

Output Format:
A single line containing N space-separated integers.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -1000000 <= arr[i] <= 1000000

questions.title: Array Forward Traversal Drill
questions.description:
Read an integer N followed by N integers and print each integer on its own line by traversing the array forward.

Input Format:
First line: integer N. Second line: N space-separated integers.

Output Format:
N lines, each containing one integer.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -1000000 <= arr[i] <= 1000000

questions.title: Array Min and Max Drill
questions.description:
Read an integer N followed by N integers and print the minimum value on the first line and the maximum value on the second line.

Input Format:
First line: integer N. Second line: N space-separated integers.

Output Format:
Two lines: first the minimum, then the maximum.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -1000000 <= arr[i] <= 1000000

questions.title: Array Reversal Print Drill
questions.description:
Read an integer N followed by N integers and print them in reverse order, space-separated, on a single line.

Input Format:
First line: integer N. Second line: N space-separated integers.

Output Format:
A single line containing N space-separated integers in reverse order.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -1000000 <= arr[i] <= 1000000

questions.title: Array Right Rotation Reversal Trick
questions.description:
A log archiver right-rotates an array of N entries by K positions using the three-reversal trick: reverse the whole array, reverse the first K elements, then reverse the remaining N-K elements. Do not use memcpy or memmove. Print the rotated array space-separated.

Input Format:
First line: integers N and K. Second line: N space-separated integers.

Output Format:
A single line with the right-rotated array, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 0 <= K <= 1000000, -1000000 <= value <= 1000000

questions.title: Array Sum Aggregation Drill
questions.description:
Read an integer N followed by N integers and print their sum.

Input Format:
First line: integer N. Second line: N space-separated integers.

Output Format:
Print the sum as a single integer on its own line.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -1000000 <= arr[i] <= 1000000

questions.title: Array of Student Records
questions.description:
Define a struct Student with members id and age. Read n, then n pairs of (id, age). Print each pair on its own line in the format "<id> <age>".

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Next n lines: each line has two space-separated integers (id and age).

Output Format:
n lines, each containing "<id> <age>".

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= id <= 10^9, 1 <= age <= 150

questions.title: Atoi Token Conversion
questions.description:
A CLI tool reads a single numeric argument and prints its value doubled. Simulate argv[1] by reading one token from stdin and convert it to int using atoi. Print 2 * value. If the token is not a valid integer, atoi returns 0 and the output is 0.

Input Format:
A single token (a numeric string).

Output Format:
A single integer: 2 * atoi(token).

Constraints:
Token represents a value in [-10^9, 10^9]

questions.title: Attendance Sheet Printer
questions.description:
A teacher reads the number of students in a class followed by their single-word names, and prints an indexed attendance sheet.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N (number of students).
Next N lines: one single-word NAME per line.

Output Format:
Print N lines, the i-th line containing "<i>. <NAME>" (1-based index).

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= length(NAME) <= 50

questions.title: Auto-Base Integer Argument Converter
questions.description:
A CLI tool reads a single numeric token and converts it to a long using auto base detection: if the token starts with "0x" or "0X" parse as base 16; else if it starts with '0' (and has more digits) parse as base 8; else parse as base 10. Use strtol with base 0 if convenient, or implement the detection manually with strcmp/strstr. Print the resulting long. Do not use sscanf for the conversion.

Input Format:
A single token.

Output Format:
A single long integer: the converted value.

Constraints:
Token length <= 32, value fits in long

questions.title: Average Speed Calculator
questions.description:
A trip computer reads the distance traveled and the time taken, then prints the average speed by calling a function speed that returns distance / time (and 0.0 when time is 0 to avoid division by zero).

Input Format:
Two space-separated floating-point values: DISTANCE and TIME.

Output Format:
Print the average speed to two decimals.

Constraints:
0.0 <= DISTANCE <= 1000000.0, 0.0 <= TIME <= 100000.0

questions.title: BMI Health Category Reporter
questions.description:
A health clinic records the weight (kg) and height (m) of N patients and computes each patient's BMI = weight / (height * height). It then classifies them:
- BMI < 18.5: Underweight
- 18.5 to 24.9: Normal
- 25 to 29.9: Overweight
- 30 or above: Obese

After processing all patients, print the four category counts.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Next N lines: two space-separated floating-point values WEIGHT and HEIGHT.

Output Format:
Print four lines:
"Underweight: <count>"
"Normal: <count>"
"Overweight: <count>"
"Obese: <count>"

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1.0 <= WEIGHT <= 500.0, 0.5 <= HEIGHT <= 3.0

questions.title: Bank Account Withdrawal Check
questions.description:
A bank account has an account number and an integer balance. Read the account number, the current balance, and a withdrawal amount. If the balance is sufficient, deduct the withdrawal and print the new balance; otherwise print "INSUFFICIENT".

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated integers: account_no balance withdrawal.

Output Format:
The new balance, or "INSUFFICIENT".

Constraints:
1 <= account_no <= 10^9, 0 <= balance <= 10^9, 0 <= withdrawal <= 10^9

questions.title: Bank Interest via Rate Macro
questions.description:
A bank defines INTEREST_RATE as 5 (percent). Read a principal P (integer), compute the integer interest as P * INTEREST_RATE / 100, and print it.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer P.

Output Format:
The integer interest.

Constraints:
1 <= P <= 10^6

questions.title: Bank Running Balance Reporter
questions.description:
A bank records N transactions where positive values are deposits and negative values are withdrawals. Traverse the transaction array and print the running balance after each transaction, one balance per line.

Input Format:
First line: integer N. Second line: N space-separated integer transactions.

Output Format:
N lines, each containing the running balance after that transaction.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -1000000 <= transaction <= 1000000, final balance fits in a 64-bit signed integer

questions.title: Banking Transaction Processor
questions.description:
A bank processes N transactions against an account starting with a balance of 0.0. Each transaction has a type letter and an amount:
- 'D' (deposit): add the amount to the balance.
- 'W' (withdraw): subtract the amount only if it does not exceed the balance; otherwise ignore.
- 'B' (balance check): no change to the balance.

Use a switch on the type, with a nested if for the withdrawal case. Print the final balance.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Next N lines: a character TYPE and a floating-point AMOUNT, space-separated.

Output Format:
Print the final balance to two decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 0.0 <= AMOUNT <= 1000000.0

questions.title: Battery Voltage Range Classifier
questions.description:
A battery management system reads N voltage readings and classifies each reading as Low (strictly below 3.0 V), Normal (3.0 V up to and including 4.2 V), or High (strictly above 4.2 V). At the end it reports the three counts.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N (number of readings).
Next N lines: a single floating-point voltage value.

Output Format:
Line 1: "Low: <count>"
Line 2: "Normal: <count>"
Line 3: "High: <count>"

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100000, 0.0 <= voltage <= 12.0

questions.title: Binary Int Archive Drill
questions.description:
Read an integer n from stdin. Open /tmp/atom_day20_binint.bin in binary write mode ("wb") and write the integer using fwrite, then close. Reopen the file in binary read mode ("rb"), use fread to read the integer back, then close. Print BIN <value>.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
A single line: BIN <n>.

Constraints:
-100000 <= n <= 100000

questions.title: Binary Inventory Database Query
questions.description:
A store maintains an inventory database persisted as a binary file of structs. Read N then N records (id, qty, price as a double) from stdin. Define a struct with int id, int qty, double price. Open /tmp/atom_day20_invent.bin in binary write mode and write all records with one fwrite, then close. Reopen in binary read mode, read the records back with one fread, then close. Compute the total inventory value (sum of qty * price over all records) and find the id of the record whose qty*price is the largest (use a manual loop, no qsort). Print VALUE <v.xx> TOP_ID <id>.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N. Next N lines: <id> <qty> <price> per line (price is a floating-point number).

Output Format:
A single line: VALUE <v.xx> TOP_ID <id> with two decimals for the value.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= id <= 99999, 0 <= qty <= 10000, 0.00 <= price <= 10000.00

questions.title: Binary Student Record Archive
questions.description:
A school persists student records (roll number and marks) as a binary file for compact storage. Read N then N pairs (roll, marks) from stdin. Define a struct with two int members (roll and marks). Open /tmp/atom_day20_studrec.bin in binary write mode, write all N records with a single fwrite call, then close. Reopen in binary read mode, read the records back with a single fread call into a local array, then close. Print TOTAL <total_marks> COUNT <n_read>.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N. Next N lines: <roll> <marks> per line.

Output Format:
A single line: TOTAL <sum_of_marks> COUNT <n_read>.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= roll <= 99999, 0 <= marks <= 100

questions.title: Bitwise AND Drill
questions.description:
Read two non-negative integers and print the result of their bitwise AND.

Input Format:
Two space-separated non-negative integers A and B.

Output Format:
Print A & B on its own line.

Constraints:
0 <= A, B <= 1000000

questions.title: Bitwise AND of Two Unsigned Integers
questions.description:
Read two unsigned 32-bit integers and print their bitwise AND.

Input Format:
Two space-separated unsigned 32-bit integers a and b.

Output Format:
A single integer: a & b.

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 4294967295

questions.title: Bitwise NOT of an Unsigned Integer
questions.description:
Read one unsigned 32-bit integer and print its bitwise complement (one's complement).

Input Format:
A single unsigned 32-bit integer n.

Output Format:
A single integer: ~n.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 4294967295

questions.title: Bitwise OR Drill
questions.description:
Read two non-negative integers and print the result of their bitwise OR.

Input Format:
Two space-separated non-negative integers A and B.

Output Format:
Print A | B on its own line.

Constraints:
0 <= A, B <= 1000000

questions.title: Bitwise OR of Two Unsigned Integers
questions.description:
Read two unsigned 32-bit integers and print their bitwise OR.

Input Format:
Two space-separated unsigned 32-bit integers a and b.

Output Format:
A single integer: a | b.

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 4294967295

questions.title: Bitwise Parity Bit Counter
questions.description:
A communications protocol computes the parity of a 32-bit word by counting the number of set bits. Read an unsigned integer and print the count of 1 bits in its binary representation, using a while loop and bitwise operators.

Input Format:
A single unsigned integer N.

Output Format:
Print the count of 1 bits.

Constraints:
0 <= N <= 4294967295

questions.title: Bitwise Permission Flag Packer
questions.description:
A file-system permission tool packs four permission bits (read, write, execute, admin) into a single byte using bit shifts and bitwise OR. Each input is 0 or 1. The packed layout is: read in bit 3, write in bit 2, execute in bit 1, admin in bit 0.

Input Format:
Four space-separated 0/1 values: R W X A.

Output Format:
Print the packed integer value.

Constraints:
Each of R, W, X, A is 0 or 1
questions.inputconstrains: Each of R, W, X, A is 0 or 1

questions.title: Bitwise RGB Color Blender
questions.description:
A graphics utility blends two colors stored as packed 24-bit RGB integers (red in bits 16-23, green in bits 8-15, blue in bits 0-7). For each channel compute the integer average of the two colors, then repack and print the blended color.

Input Format:
Two space-separated non-negative integers C1 and C2 (each in [0, 16777215]).

Output Format:
Print the blended packed RGB value on its own line.

Constraints:
0 <= C1, C2 <= 16777215

questions.title: Bitwise Shift Encoder
questions.description:
A simple obfuscation tool reads a byte value and a non-negative shift amount, then prints the value after a left bitwise shift. Use the shift operator directly.

Input Format:
Two space-separated non-negative integers V and N.

Output Format:
Print V << N on its own line.

Constraints:
0 <= V <= 65535, 0 <= N <= 15

questions.title: Bitwise Unsigned Division Algorithm
questions.description:
Implement unsigned 32-bit integer division using bit shifts and subtractions (the restoring division algorithm). Read dividend a and divisor b. Print the quotient a / b. Handle b = 0 by printing -1. Do not use the /, %, or * operators; use shifts and comparisons.

Input Format:
Two space-separated unsigned 32-bit integers a and b.

Output Format:
A single integer: the quotient, or -1 if b is 0.

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 4294967295

questions.title: Bitwise XOR of Two Unsigned Integers
questions.description:
Read two unsigned 32-bit integers and print their bitwise XOR.

Input Format:
Two space-separated unsigned 32-bit integers a and b.

Output Format:
A single integer: a ^ b.

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 4294967295

questions.title: Boarding Pass Passenger Echo
questions.description:
An airport kiosk reads a passenger's first name and a flight code (both single tokens) from stdin and prints a boarding pass header line.

Input Format:
A single line containing two space-separated tokens: the passenger's first name and the flight code.

Output Format:
A single line in the form "Passenger <name> Flight <flight>".

Constraints:
1 <= length of each token <= 50
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of each token <= 50, no spaces inside tokens

questions.title: Bonus Tier via Nested Ifdef
questions.description:
A feature-flag system uses nested #ifdef/#else to pick a bonus tier. PRO_FEATURE is NOT defined; BASIC_FEATURE IS defined; the bonus is 10. Read an integer n, then print n + BONUS.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n.

Output Format:
The value n + 10.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= n <= 10^9

questions.title: Book Loan Status Decoder
questions.description:
A library reads N book records. Each record contains a status code (1 = Available, 2 = Borrowed, 3 = Reserved, 4 = Lost) and a member type (0 = Guest, 1 = Member). Based on the status and member type, print one action per book:
- Available: "Available"
- Borrowed: "Return" if Member, "Denied" if Guest
- Reserved: "Pickup" if Member, "Denied" if Guest
- Lost: "Report"
- any other status: "Invalid"

Use a switch on the status with nested if statements for member-only cases.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Next N lines: two space-separated integers STATUS and MEMBER.

Output Format:
Print one action per line, in input order.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, STATUS is an integer, MEMBER is 0 or 1
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= N <= 1000, STATUS is an integer, MEMBER is 0 or 1

questions.title: Bootloader Config Pointer Check
questions.description:
A bootloader reads a flag f and a config value v. If f is 1, the config pointer is set to &v; if f is 0, the pointer stays NULL. Print the dereferenced value when f is 1, otherwise print "FAIL".

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers: f and v.

Output Format:
The value v (when f == 1) or "FAIL" (when f == 0).

Constraints:
f in {0, 1}, -10^9 <= v <= 10^9

questions.title: Bounded Frequency Counter
questions.description:
A survey collects N integer responses, each guaranteed to be in the range [1, K]. Count how many times each value 1..K appears. Initialize a frequency array, then print K lines, line i containing the count of value i.

Input Format:
First line: integers N and K. Second line: N space-separated integers each in [1, K].

Output Format:
K lines, each containing the frequency of value i (for i from 1 to K).

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= K <= 1000, each response in [1, K]
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= K <= 1000, each response in [1, K]

questions.title: Build Mode Banner via Ifdef
questions.description:
A build system uses #ifdef EXTERNAL_API to switch the build banner. In this build EXTERNAL_API is NOT defined, so the banner is "BUILTIN <n>". Read an integer n, then print the banner.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n.

Output Format:
The string "BUILTIN <n>".

Constraints:
-10^9 <= n <= 10^9

questions.title: Cafe Order Receipt Printer
questions.description:
A small cafe prints a basic receipt for every order. Read the item name and its price, then print a two-line receipt.

Input Format:
Line 1: a single-word item name ITEM.
Line 2: the price PRICE as a floating-point number.

Output Format:
Line 1: "Item: <ITEM>"
Line 2: "Price: <PRICE>" with PRICE formatted to two decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= length(ITEM) <= 50 and 0.0 <= PRICE <= 100000.0

questions.title: Callback Handler Dispatch
questions.description:
A GUI framework declares typedef void (*Handler)(int, int*). Define handlers handler_add (adds v to *out), handler_mul (multiplies *out by v), handler_sub (subtracts v from *out). Read op (1=add, 2=mul, 3=sub), accumulator, and value. Dispatch via a Handler and print the final accumulator value. Default op acts as add. Do not use pow or goto.

Input Format:
Three space-separated integers: op accumulator value.

Output Format:
A single integer: the new accumulator value.

Constraints:
-1000 <= accumulator, value <= 1000

questions.title: Camel to Snake Identifier Formatter
questions.description:
A code formatter converts a camelCase identifier (single word) to snake_case. For each uppercase letter encountered, output an underscore followed by the lowercase version (using tolower from ctype.h). Lowercase letters and other characters pass through unchanged. Use isupper from ctype.h to detect uppercase letters — do NOT use 'A' or 'a' character literals for case detection.

Input Format:
A single line containing one camelCase identifier.

Output Format:
The snake_case version of the identifier on its own line.

Constraints:
1 <= identifier length <= 100

questions.title: Cargo Container Weight Recursive Sum
questions.description:
A shipping dock records the weight of N cargo containers in an array. The supervisor insists the total weight be computed using recursion only (no loops anywhere in the program, including for reading input). Print the total weight.

Input Format:
First line: integer N. Second line: N space-separated integer weights.

Output Format:
Print the total weight as a single integer on its own line.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -1000000 <= weight <= 1000000

questions.title: Cartesian Quadrant Finder
questions.description:
A geometry tool reads the (x, y) coordinates of a point and identifies which quadrant it lies in using an if-else if ladder.

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers X and Y.

Output Format:
Print "Quadrant 1", "Quadrant 2", "Quadrant 3", "Quadrant 4", "Axis", or "Origin".

Constraints:
-10000 <= X, Y <= 10000

questions.title: Celsius Fahrenheit Converter
questions.description:
A weather app reads a temperature in Celsius and prints the equivalent Fahrenheit value by calling a function to_fahrenheit that performs the conversion F = C * 9/5 + 32.

Input Format:
A single floating-point value C (degrees Celsius).

Output Format:
Print the Fahrenheit value to two decimals.

Constraints:
-100.0 <= C <= 200.0

questions.title: Celsius Temperature Display
questions.description:
A weather station reads a temperature in degrees Celsius and prints it in a fixed-format line.

Input Format:
A single floating-point value C representing degrees Celsius.

Output Format:
Print "T = <C> C" with C formatted to two decimals.

Constraints:
-100.0 <= C <= 200.0

questions.title: Character Echo Drill
questions.description:
Read a single character from standard input and print it back on its own line.

Input Format:
A single character C.

Output Format:
Print the character C on its own line.

Constraints:

1 to 40 tokens

Read an integer N, then N integers, then a target value. Print the 0-based index of the first occurrence of the target, or -1 if not found.

Input Format:
First line: integer N. Second line: N space-separated integers. Third line: target integer.

Output Format:
A single integer index, or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -1000000 <= arr[i] <= 1000000

questions.title: Log Buffer Cleanup Reporter
questions.description:
A logging system allocates a buffer of n+1 characters via malloc, fills positions 0..n-1 with the letters 'A', 'B', 'C', ... (capital letters), null-terminates at position n, prints the buffer string, then frees the buffer and prints the word "freed".

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n.

Output Format:
Two lines: the buffer string, then the word "freed".

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 26

questions.title: Log File Character Frequency Reporter
questions.description:
A log scanner must classify characters in a one-line log message. Read the line from stdin using a getchar loop (stopping at newline or EOF, no fgets allowed). Open /tmp/atom_day20_log.txt in write mode, write the line followed by a newline using fprintf, then close. Reopen the file in read mode, scan every character with fgetc, count digit characters and alphabetic characters (manually, not via ctype.h helpers), then close and print DIGITS <d> ALPHA <a>.

Input Format:
A single line of text (may contain interior spaces).

Output Format:
A single line: DIGITS <d> ALPHA <a>.

Constraints:
Line length 1..1023

questions.title: Logical Gate Emulator
questions.description:
A digital circuit simulator reads four boolean inputs (each 0 or 1) labeled a, b, c, d and evaluates the boolean expression (a AND b) OR (c AND NOT d) using C's logical operators. Print 1 if the expression is true, 0 otherwise.

Input Format:
Four space-separated 0/1 integers A B C D.

Output Format:
Print 1 or 0.

Constraints:
Each input is 0 or 1

questions.title: Login Lockout After Attempts
questions.description:
A login system locks the account after 3 failed attempts. Read the number of failed attempts n. If n >= 3 print LOCKED; otherwise print ALLOWED attempts_left where attempts_left = 3 - n.

Input Format:
A single integer n (failed attempts so far).

Output Format:
A single line: LOCKED or ALLOWED attempts_left.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 10

questions.title: Long Option Parser with Equals
questions.description:
A CLI accepts long-form options --verbose, --quiet, and --count=N. Read tokens; track whether --verbose was last seen among verbose/quiet (default quiet), and the last value of --count (default 0). Print two lines: mode (VERBOSE or QUIET) and count. Use strstr to find the --count prefix. Do not use strtok.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated tokens.

Output Format:
Line 1: VERBOSE or QUIET. Line 2: count value.

Constraints:
1 to 30 tokens

questions.title: Manhattan Distance from Origin
questions.description:
A navigation tool computes the Manhattan distance from the origin to a point. Define a struct Point with members x and y. Pass the struct by value to a helper function that returns |x| + |y|.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers x and y.

Output Format:
The Manhattan distance as a single integer.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= x, y <= 10^9

questions.title: Manual Power Function
questions.description:
A math utility reads a base and a non-negative exponent, then prints base raised to that exponent by calling a function power that computes the result with a for loop (no math library).

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers BASE and EXP.

Output Format:
Print BASE^EXP as a 64-bit integer.

Constraints:
-1000 <= BASE <= 1000, 0 <= EXP <= 30

questions.title: Manual String Equality Drill
questions.description:
Read two words and determine whether they are equal by comparing them character-by-character. Do NOT use strcmp. Print "Equal" if they match exactly (same length and same characters), otherwise print "NotEqual".

Input Format:
A single line containing two space-separated words.

Output Format:
The word "Equal" or "NotEqual" on its own line.

Constraints:
1 <= length of each word <= 1000
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of each word <= 1000, no spaces inside words

questions.title: Manual String Length Counter
questions.description:
Read a single word and count its length manually by traversing characters until the null terminator. Do NOT use strlen. Print the length as an integer.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word (no spaces).

Output Format:
A single integer — the length of the word.

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 1000

questions.title: Matrix 90 Degree Clockwise Rotation
questions.description:
An image rotation tool rotates an N x N matrix 90 degrees clockwise by first transposing it in-place, then reversing each row. Print the rotated matrix. Do not use memcpy or memmove.

Input Format:
First line: integer N. Next N lines: N space-separated integers.

Output Format:
N lines, each with N space-separated integers (rotated matrix).

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, -1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Matrix Addition Drill
questions.description:
Read two R x C matrices A and B and print their sum (A + B) in the same R x C layout.

Input Format:
First line: integers R and C. Next R lines: matrix A. Then R lines: matrix B.

Output Format:
R lines, each with C space-separated integers.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 100, -1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Matrix Column Maximum Drill
questions.description:
Read an R x C matrix and print the maximum value of each column, one per line.

Input Format:
First line: integers R and C. Next R lines: C space-separated integers each.

Output Format:
C lines, each containing the maximum of the corresponding column.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 100, -1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Matrix Column Sums Reporter
questions.description:
A meteorologist has an R x C grid of rainfall readings. Compute the sum of each column and print them space-separated on one line. Do not use memcpy.

Input Format:
First line: integers R and C. Next R lines: C space-separated integers.

Output Format:
A single line with C space-separated column sums.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 100, 0 <= value <= 10000

questions.title: Matrix Echo Drill
questions.description:
Read a matrix of R rows and C columns and print it back exactly, with rows on separate lines and space-separated values.

Input Format:
First line: integers R and C. Next R lines: C space-separated integers each.

Output Format:
R lines, each with C space-separated integers.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 100, -1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Matrix Main Diagonal Printer Drill
questions.description:
Read a square N x N matrix and print its main diagonal elements on one line, space-separated.

Input Format:
First line: integer N. Next N lines: N space-separated integers each.

Output Format:
A single line with N space-separated integers (the main diagonal).

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, -1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Matrix Multiplication Calculator
questions.description:
A scientific computing tool multiplies an M x N matrix A by an N x P matrix B and prints the resulting M x P matrix. Do not use memcpy. Use a triple-nested loop.

Input Format:
First line: three integers M N P. Next M lines: N space-separated integers (matrix A). Next N lines: P space-separated integers (matrix B).

Output Format:
M lines, each with P space-separated integers (the product matrix).

Constraints:
1 <= M, N, P <= 50, -1000 <= value <= 1000, each product element fits in a 64-bit signed integer

questions.title: Matrix Row Sum Drill
questions.description:
Read an R x C matrix and print the sum of each row, one sum per line.

Input Format:
First line: integers R and C. Next R lines: C space-separated integers each.

Output Format:
R lines, each containing the sum of the corresponding row.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 100, -1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Matrix Subtraction Reporter
questions.description:
A finance tool subtracts matrix B (expenses) from matrix A (revenues) for each cell of an R x C budget grid. Print the resulting matrix A - B. Do not use memcpy or memmove.

Input Format:
First line: integers R and C. Next R lines: matrix A. Then R lines: matrix B.

Output Format:
R lines, each with C space-separated integers.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 100, -10000 <= value <= 10000

questions.title: Matrix Total Sum Drill
questions.description:
Read an R x C matrix and print the sum of all its elements on a single line.

Input Format:
First line: integers R and C. Next R lines: C space-separated integers each.

Output Format:
A single integer: the total sum.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 100, -1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Matrix Trace Calculator
questions.description:
A linear algebra class computes the trace of a square matrix (sum of main diagonal elements). Read the matrix and print its trace. Do not use qsort.

Input Format:
First line: integer N. Next N lines: N space-separated integers.

Output Format:
A single integer: the trace.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, -1000 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Matrix Trace via Typedef
questions.description:
Define typedef int Matrix[3][3]. Read 9 integers row-by-row, compute the trace (sum of diagonal m[0][0] + m[1][1] + m[2][2]) and print it. Do not use pow or goto.

Input Format:
Three lines of three space-separated integers each.

Output Format:
A single integer: the trace.

Constraints:
-1000 <= matrix values <= 1000

questions.title: Max Index via Pointer Walk
questions.description:
A streaming service has n subscriber usage values. Find the 0-based index of the maximum usage using pointer arithmetic. If there is a tie, return the smallest index.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
The 0-based index of the maximum value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -10^4 <= value <= 10^4

questions.title: Max Numeric Argument Finder
questions.description:
A utility reads numeric arguments and prints the maximum value. Simulate argv by reading space-separated integer tokens from stdin. Print the maximum integer. At least one valid integer is guaranteed.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated integer tokens.

Output Format:
A single integer: the maximum value.

Constraints:
1 to 100 tokens, each in [-10^9, 10^9]

questions.title: Max of Two via Macro Function
questions.description:
A math utility defines a macro MAX(a, b). Read two integers a and b, then print the maximum using MAX(a, b).

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers.

Output Format:
The maximum of a and b.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= a, b <= 10^9

questions.title: Maximum of Two via Function
questions.description:
Read two integers and print the larger one by calling a function named max_of_two that returns the maximum of its two int parameters.

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers A and B.

Output Format:
Print the maximum of A and B.

Constraints:
-1000000 <= A, B <= 1000000

questions.title: Mirrored Number Ladder
questions.description:
A parking-lot floor numbering sign shows a mirrored number ladder. Row i (1-indexed) has 2*i-1 cells containing i, i-1, ..., 1, ..., i-1, i — i.e. descending from i to 1 then ascending back to i. Build the row in an integer array then print it (no memcpy/strcpy).

Input Format:
A single integer N.

Output Format:
N lines of mirrored numbers, space-separated within each row.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100

questions.title: Modular Calculator Suite
questions.description:
A modular calculator reads N and prints three values computed by three separate functions:
- factorial(N) = N!
- square(N) = N * N
- cube(N) = N * N * N

Use three function definitions above main to demonstrate modular design.

Input Format:
A single integer N.

Output Format:
Print three lines:
"Factorial: <F>"
"Square: <S>"
"Cube: <C>"

Constraints:
0 <= N <= 20

questions.title: Modular Day-of-Year Calculator
questions.description:
A date utility reads a day, month, and year, then prints the day-of-year (1 to 366) by calling a function day_of_year that uses two helper functions: is_leap_year (returns 1 if the year is a leap year) and days_in_month (returns the number of days in a given month, accounting for leap years).

Input Format:
Three space-separated integers: DAY, MONTH, YEAR.

Output Format:
Print the day-of-year as an integer.

Constraints:
1 <= DAY <= 31, 1 <= MONTH <= 12, 1 <= YEAR <= 9999. The input is guaranteed to be a valid date.

questions.title: Modular Number Theory Suite
questions.description:
A number-theory explorer reads an integer N and prints three classifications computed by three separate functions:
- is_prime(N): "Yes" if N is prime, else "No"
- is_armstrong(N): "Yes" if N is an Armstrong number (sum of its digits each raised to the digit count equals N), else "No"
- is_perfect(N): "Yes" if N equals the sum of its proper divisors, else "No"

Modular design is required; do not use the math library.

Input Format:
A single integer N.

Output Format:
Print three lines:
"Prime: <Yes|No>"
"Armstrong: <Yes|No>"
"Perfect: <Yes|No>"

Constraints:
0 <= N <= 100000

questions.title: Modular Statistics Reporter
questions.description:
A statistics tool reads N floating-point values into an array and reports the minimum, maximum, sum, and average by calling three helper functions: find_min, find_max, and compute_sum. Modular design is required.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Next N lines: one floating-point value each.

Output Format:
Print four lines:
"Min: <min>"
"Max: <max>"
"Sum: <sum>"
"Avg: <avg>"
with each value to two decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -1000000.0 <= value <= 1000000.0

questions.title: Modular Triangle Validator
questions.description:
A geometry tool reads three side lengths and prints the area of the triangle. Use two helper functions: is_valid_triangle (returns 1 if sides form a valid triangle, 0 otherwise) and triangle_area (returns 0.0 if invalid; otherwise applies Heron's formula and computes the square root via Newton's method, without using math.h).

Input Format:
Three space-separated integers A, B, C (side lengths).

Output Format:
Print the area to two decimals. Print 0.00 if the sides do not form a valid triangle.

Constraints:
1 <= A, B, C <= 10000

questions.title: Modulo Remainder Drill
questions.description:
Read two integers A and B and print the remainder of A divided by B using the modulo operator.

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers A and B.

Output Format:
Print A % B on its own line.

Constraints:
-1000000 <= A <= 1000000, 1 <= B <= 1000000

questions.title: Month Days Printer
questions.description:
A calendar utility reads a month number (1-12) and prints how many days that month has in a non-leap year. Use a switch statement that groups cases by fall-through.

Input Format:
A single integer MONTH in [1, 12].

Output Format:
Print the number of days (28, 30, or 31) for the month, or 0 if the month is out of range.

Constraints:
MONTH is an integer.

questions.title: Move Point via Struct Pointer
questions.description:
A graphics engine moves a Point by (dx, dy) using a helper that takes a struct Point pointer. Read x, y, dx, dy, then print the new coordinates.

Input Format:
A single line with four space-separated integers: x y dx dy.

Output Format:
The new x and y space-separated.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= x, y, dx, dy <= 10^9

questions.title: Multi-Field Validation with Errno
questions.description:
A form validator checks three fields: age (0-120), score (0-100), grade (1-5). Read age score grade. If any field is out of range, set errno=EINVAL and print INVALID field_name errno_value for the FIRST failing field. Otherwise print ALL_OK. Do not use goto or abort.

Input Format:
Three space-separated integers: age, score, grade.

Output Format:
A single line: ALL_OK, or INVALID field_name errno_value.

Constraints:
-100 <= age, score, grade <= 200

questions.title: Multi-Flag Configuration Parser
questions.description:
A CLI tool accepts flags -v (verbose), -q (quiet) and -n NUM (count). Read space-separated tokens simulating argv. Track which of -v and -q were seen, and the last value of -n (default 0). Output three lines: VERBOSE or QUIET (whichever was the LAST among -v/-q seen, default QUIET), then the count value, then the total number of tokens parsed. Do not use strstr for flag detection — use strcmp.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated tokens.

Output Format:
Line 1: VERBOSE or QUIET. Line 2: the count value. Line 3: total token count.

Constraints:
1 to 50 tokens

questions.title: Multi-Mode File Error Resilience
questions.description:
A resilient file manager tests both its success path and its failure path. Read two integers n and c from stdin. When c == 0, attempt to open the (never-created) file /tmp/atom_day20_no_such_file.txt in read mode; if fopen returns NULL (as it should) print OPEN_FAILED and stop; otherwise close the file and print UNEXPECTED. When c == 1, open /tmp/atom_day20_resilient.txt in write mode (checking for NULL), write n via fprintf, close, reopen in read mode (checking for NULL), parse the integer back manually with fgetc (digit by digit, respecting a leading minus sign), close, and print FINAL <value>.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers: n and c.

Output Format:
A single line: OPEN_FAILED (when c == 0) or FINAL <n> (when c == 1).

Constraints:
-100000 <= n <= 100000, c in {0, 1}

questions.title: Multiplication Table Row Printer
questions.description:
Read an integer N and print N*1, N*2, ..., N*10 each on its own line using a for loop.

Input Format:
A single integer N.

Output Format:
Print 10 lines, the i-th containing N * i for i from 1 to 10.

Constraints:
-1000 <= N <= 1000

questions.title: Multiplication Table Triangle
questions.description:
A classroom desk chart shows a multiplication triangle. Row i (1-indexed) contains i*1, i*2, ..., i*i, stored in an array and printed space-separated.

Input Format:
A single integer N.

Output Format:
N lines. Line i contains i multiples of i space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100

questions.title: Name Banner Printer
questions.description:
Read a single-word name and print it wrapped in a banner of equals signs.

Input Format:
A single-word string NAME (no spaces).

Output Format:
Print the line "=== NAME ===" exactly.

Constraints:
1 <= length(NAME) <= 50

questions.title: Nested Date in Event
questions.description:
Define a struct Date with members day, month, year. Define a struct Event that contains a Date as a nested member. Read the day, month, and year, then print them in day/month/year format.

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated integers: day month year.

Output Format:
The string "<day>/<month>/<year>".

Constraints:
1 <= day <= 31, 1 <= month <= 12, 1900 <= year <= 2100

questions.title: Null Pointer Guard Drill
questions.description:
Read an integer n. If n is non-zero, set a pointer p to &n; otherwise set p to NULL. Print the value via *p when p is not NULL, otherwise print "NULL".

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n.

Output Format:
The value of n (when non-zero) or the string "NULL" (when n == 0).

Constraints:
-10^9 <= n <= 10^9

questions.title: Number Row Echo Drill
questions.description:
Read a positive integer N and store the values 1, 2, ..., N into an integer array. Print the row on a single line with the numbers space-separated.

Input Format:
A single integer N.

Output Format:
A single line containing N space-separated integers from 1 to N.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100

questions.title: Number Triangle Echo
questions.description:
Read a positive integer N and print N rows. Row i (1-indexed) contains the integers 1 through i stored in an array and printed space-separated.

Input Format:
A single integer N.

Output Format:
N lines. Line i contains i space-separated integers from 1 to i.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100

questions.title: Numerology Digital Root Calculator
questions.description:
A numerology app reduces a number to its digital root by repeatedly summing its digits until a single digit remains. Use recursive functions only (no loops anywhere) to compute the digital root. For input 0, output 0.

Input Format:
A single non-negative integer N.

Output Format:
Print the digital root (a single digit 0-9) on its own line.

Constraints:
0 <= N <= 1000000000000000000

questions.title: Opcode Validator with Range Errors
questions.description:
A calculator CLI takes an opcode (1-5) and a value. Opcode 1 doubles, 2 triples, 3 squares, 4 negates, 5 zeroes. If the opcode is out of [1,5], set errno=EINVAL (22) and print OP_ERR errno_value. If the result exceeds [-1000, 1000], set errno=ERANGE (34) and print RANGE_ERR errno_value. Otherwise print OK result. Do not use goto or abort.

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers: opcode and value.

Output Format:
A single line: OK result, OP_ERR errno_value, or RANGE_ERR errno_value.

Constraints:
-1000 <= value <= 1000, opcode in [-1, 10]

questions.title: Operator Args Mini Calculator
questions.description:
A calculator CLI takes the operator as the first argument and applies it to all remaining numeric arguments. Read tokens: first is one of + - * (the operator). Remaining tokens are integers. Compute the result of applying the operator left-to-right (e.g. + means sum, - means first minus rest, * means product). For division-by-zero or no operands, print 0. Do not use pow or sprintf. Use atoi for conversion.

Input Format:
First token: operator (+, -, *). Remaining tokens: integers.

Output Format:
A single integer: the computed result.

Constraints:
1 to 20 numeric operands, values fit in 32-bit int

questions.title: Order Status Transition Machine
questions.description:
An e-commerce backend uses enum OrderStatus { ORDER_PENDING, ORDER_PROCESSING, ORDER_SHIPPED, ORDER_DELIVERED, ORDER_CANCELLED }. Read a current status (0-4) and print the next status according to the rules: PENDING->PROCESSING, PROCESSING->SHIPPED, SHIPPED->DELIVERED, DELIVERED->DELIVERED (terminal), CANCELLED->CANCELLED (terminal). Do not use pow or goto.

Input Format:
A single integer current status (0-4).

Output Format:
A single integer: the next status.

Constraints:
0 <= status <= 4

questions.title: PAN Number Format Validator
questions.description:
An Indian PAN (Permanent Account Number) is a 10-character code with a strict format: positions 1-5 are uppercase letters (A-Z), positions 6-9 are digits (0-9), and position 10 is an uppercase letter. Read a PAN string (single token) and validate this format by manual traversal. Do NOT use strlen or any of the is* functions (isalpha, isdigit, isalnum) — check character ranges with 'A'-'Z' and '0'-'9' comparisons and the logical AND operator. Print "VALID" or "INVALID".

Input Format:
A single line containing one PAN string.

Output Format:
A single line: "VALID" or "INVALID".

Constraints:
1 <= PAN length <= 30

questions.title: Packed Struct Size via Pragma
questions.description:
A library uses #pragma pack(push, 1) to control struct alignment. Define a struct Packed with a char and an int. Read an integer n, then print "<n> <sizeof>" where <sizeof> is the byte size of the packed struct.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n.

Output Format:
The string "<n> <sizeof>" (sizeof is the byte size of struct Packed).

Constraints:
-10^9 <= n <= 10^9

questions.title: Palindrome Word Check Drill
questions.description:
Given a single non-empty word of lowercase English letters, determine whether it is a palindrome (reads the same forward and backward).

Input Format:
A single line containing one word (lowercase letters only).

Output Format:
Print "Yes" if the word is a palindrome, otherwise print "No".

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 1000

questions.title: Parity of Byte Stream
questions.description:
A communication channel transmits bytes and a parity bit is computed as the XOR of all bits in each byte (odd parity = 1 if odd number of bits set). Read n bytes (as unsigned 32-bit values, only low 8 bits used) and print 1 if the total number of set bits across all bytes is odd, 0 if even. Use the XOR reduction idiom.

Input Format:
First line: n. Second line: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
A single integer: 1 for odd parity, 0 for even.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, each value in [0, 255]

questions.title: Parking Minutes Round-Up Calculator
questions.description:
A parking garage charges by the hour, rounding any partial hour up. Read the total minutes parked and print the number of billable hours. Use integer arithmetic (no math library).

Input Format:
A single integer MINUTES.

Output Format:
Print the billable hours as an integer (ceiling of MINUTES / 60).

Constraints:
0 <= MINUTES <= 100000

questions.title: Pascal Triangle Row Cache
questions.description:
A mathematics exhibit prints Pascal's triangle using a single 1D array cache. Start with pascal[0] = 1 and all others 0. For each row i (0-indexed) update in place: for j from i down to 1, pascal[j] += pascal[j-1]. Print row i after each update. Do not use memcpy or any factorial-based formula.

Input Format:
A single integer N (number of rows).

Output Format:
N lines of Pascal's triangle, each row's values space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 30

questions.title: Pascal Triangle Sierpinski Mask
questions.description:
A fractal art exhibit overlays Pascal's triangle with a Sierpinski mask. Compute each row of Pascal's triangle in a 1D array (in-place update, same approach as Pascal row cache). For each cell, if the value is odd print '*', otherwise print a space. The result is a left-aligned Sierpinski triangle of N rows. Do not use memcpy or factorial-based formulas.

Input Format:
A single integer N.

Output Format:
N lines of '*' and ' ' characters (no separators between cells).

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 30

questions.title: Pass Fail Threshold
questions.description:
Read a student's marks (out of 100) and print "Pass" if marks >= 40, otherwise "Fail".

Input Format:
A single integer MARKS.

Output Format:
Print "Pass" or "Fail".

Constraints:
0 <= MARKS <= 100

questions.title: Passport Number Builder
questions.description:
A passport office issues passport numbers in the format "PAS-<country>-<serial>" where country is a 3-letter code and serial is a 6-digit number. Declare a fixed prefix "PAS-" as an initialized string and use strcpy and strcat to assemble the final passport number. Do NOT use sprintf or snprintf.

Input Format:
A single line containing two space-separated tokens: the country code and the serial number.

Output Format:
A single line: "PAS-<country>-<serial>".

Constraints:
Country is exactly 3 uppercase letters; serial is exactly 6 digits.
questions.inputconstrains: Country is 3 uppercase letters; serial is 6 digits

questions.title: Password Retry Simulator
questions.description:
A login system stores a 4-digit PIN. It then reads up to 3 attempts. If any attempt matches the PIN, print "Unlocked" and stop reading; otherwise after 3 wrong attempts print "Locked". Use a do-while loop.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer PIN (the correct PIN).
Next lines: integer ATTEMPT values, up to 3 attempts.

Output Format:
Print "Unlocked" on the first match, or "Locked" if all 3 attempts are wrong.

Constraints:
0 <= PIN <= 9999, 0 <= ATTEMPT <= 9999

questions.title: Permission Flag Enumeration
questions.description:
A file system uses enum Flag { FLAG_A=1<<0, FLAG_B=1<<1, FLAG_C=1<<2, FLAG_D=1<<3 }. Read an integer bitmask n. Build a Flag value by OR'ing in each flag whose bit is set in n. Print the count of flags actually set in the resulting Flag value. Do not use pow or goto.

Input Format:
A single integer n in [0, 15].

Output Format:
A single integer: count of set flags.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 15

questions.title: Person with Nested Address
questions.description:
A person record contains a nested Address struct (street_num and city_code). Read id, street_num, and city_code into a Person, then print in the format "ID=<id> Street=<street> City=<city>".

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated integers: id street_num city_code.

Output Format:
The string "ID=<id> Street=<street> City=<city>".

Constraints:
1 <= id <= 10^6, 1 <= street_num <= 10^4, 1 <= city_code <= 999

questions.title: Playing Card Suit Lookup
questions.description:
A card game uses an enum Suit { HEARTS, DIAMONDS, CLUBS, SPADES }. Read a suit index (0-3) and print its single-letter code (H, D, C, S). For out-of-range input print ?.

Input Format:
A single integer suit index.

Output Format:
A single character code followed by a newline.

Constraints:
-1 <= suit <= 10

questions.title: Point Distance with Typedef Struct
questions.description:
Define typedef struct Point { int x, y; }. Read two points (p1 and p2, each on its own line) and print their Manhattan distance (|p1.x-p2.x| + |p1.y-p2.y|). Do not use pow or sqrt.

Input Format:
Line 1: x1 y1. Line 2: x2 y2.

Output Format:
A single integer: the Manhattan distance.

Constraints:
-1000 <= coordinates <= 1000

questions.title: Point Struct Manhattan Distance
questions.description:
Define a typedef struct Point with fields x, y. Read a single point and print its Manhattan distance from the origin (|x| + |y|).

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers x and y.

Output Format:
A single integer: |x| + |y|.

Constraints:
-1000 <= x, y <= 1000

questions.title: Pointer Arithmetic Palindrome Check
questions.description:
Check whether an array of n integers is a palindrome (reads the same forward and backward) using two pointer walkers (lo and hi). Read n then n integers, print "Yes" or "No".

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
"Yes" if palindrome, else "No".

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -10^4 <= value <= 10^4

questions.title: Pointer Array Sum Drill
questions.description:
Read n followed by n integers. Compute the sum of the integers by traversing the array with pointer arithmetic.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
The sum of the integers.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -10^4 <= each integer <= 10^4

questions.title: Pointer Offset Access Drill
questions.description:
Read three integers a, b, c into a 3-element array, then access the third element (index 2) via pointer arithmetic and print it.

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated integers.

Output Format:
The third integer printed via *(p + 2).

Constraints:
-10^9 <= each integer <= 10^9

questions.title: Pointer Swap Helper Function
questions.description:
Two players' scores a and b must be exchanged using a helper function that takes two int pointers. Read a and b, then call swap(&a, &b), then print the swapped values separated by a single space.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
The two integers after swapping, space-separated.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= a, b <= 10^9

questions.title: Pointer Table Lookup Guard
questions.description:
A database stores n integers and exposes them via an array of n pointers (each ptr[i] points to data[i]). Given a 0-based query index q, print the value via the pointer table, or print "NULL" if q is out of range.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.
Line 3: an integer query index q.

Output Format:
The value at index q, or "NULL" if q is out of range.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -10^4 <= value <= 10^4, -10^4 <= q <= 10^4

questions.title: Pointer to Pointer Drill
questions.description:
Read an integer n. Create a pointer p pointing to n and a pointer-to-pointer pp pointing to p. Print the value via double dereference **pp.

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n.

Output Format:
The value n printed via **pp.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= n <= 10^9

questions.title: Pointer to Struct Access
questions.description:
Define a struct Point with members x and y. Create a struct Point variable and a pointer to it. Read x and y into the struct via the pointer (using ->), then print the values via the pointer.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers x and y.

Output Format:
The two integers space-separated.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= x, y <= 10^9

questions.title: Post Increment Triple Printer
questions.description:
Read an integer N and print three consecutive integers starting at N, each separated by a space, using the post-increment operator.

Input Format:
A single integer N.

Output Format:
Print three integers on one line separated by single spaces: N, N+1, N+2.

Constraints:
-1000000 <= N <= 1000000

questions.title: Precedence Calculator from Tokens
questions.description:
A CLI evaluates an infix expression given as space-separated tokens: integers and operators +, -, *. Standard precedence: * binds tighter than + and -. Left-associative. Read tokens (1 to 20 numeric operands with operators between) and print the integer result. Do not use sscanf or strtok. Use strcmp for operator detection and atoi for numeric conversion.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated tokens forming a valid infix expression.

Output Format:
A single integer: the evaluated result.

Constraints:
1 to 20 operands, all values fit in 32-bit int

questions.title: Precedence-Aware Formula Evaluator
questions.description:
A scientific calculator reads four integers and evaluates the expression a * b + c * d - a using C's default operator precedence (multiplication before addition).

Input Format:
Four space-separated integers A, B, C, D.

Output Format:
Print the integer result of A * B + C * D - A.

Constraints:
-10000 <= A, B, C, D <= 10000

questions.title: Prefix Sum Range Query Processor
questions.description:
A data analyst precomputes prefix sums of an array of N integers to answer Q range-sum queries fast. For each query (l r) with 0-based inclusive indices, print the sum of arr[l..r] using prefix[r+1] - prefix[l]. Do not sort the array.

Input Format:
First line: integer N. Second line: N space-separated integers. Third line: integer Q. Next Q lines: two space-separated integers l and r.

Output Format:
Q lines, each the sum of arr[l..r].

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= Q <= 1000, 0 <= l <= r < N, -1000000 <= arr[i] <= 1000000

questions.title: Prime Check Function with Prototype
questions.description:
A primality tester reads an integer N and prints "Prime" or "Not Prime" by calling a function is_prime that returns 1 for prime and 0 otherwise. Provide an explicit function prototype for is_prime before main, and define is_prime after main.

Input Format:
A single integer N.

Output Format:
Print "Prime" or "Not Prime".

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000000

questions.title: Prime Factorization Printer
questions.description:
A factorization tool reads an integer N >= 2 and prints all of its prime factors in non-decreasing order, each on its own line. Use a while loop that divides out each prime factor as many times as possible.

Input Format:
A single integer N.

Output Format:
Print one prime factor per line, with repeats for multiplicity.

Constraints:
2 <= N <= 1000000000

questions.title: Prime Number Checker
questions.description:
A primality tester reads a positive integer N and prints "Prime" or "Not Prime" using a for loop that breaks early when a divisor is found.

Input Format:
A single integer N.

Output Format:
Print "Prime" if N is prime (greater than 1 and divisible only by 1 and itself), otherwise "Not Prime".

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000000

questions.title: Print Source Line Number
questions.description:
Use the predefined macro __LINE__ to print the source line number where it appears. Read an integer n (ignored in the output), then print the line number on its own line. (The line number is fixed by the source layout.)

Input Format:
A single line containing one integer n.

Output Format:
The line number where __LINE__ is used.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= n <= 10^9

questions.title: Print Struct Point Members
questions.description:
Define a struct Point with members x and y. Read two integers x and y, store them in a struct Point variable, then print them space-separated.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers x and y.

Output Format:
The two integers space-separated.

Constraints:
-10^9 <= x, y <= 10^9

questions.title: Process State Machine via Enum
questions.description:
A process scheduler uses enum State { STATE_IDLE, STATE_ACTIVE, STATE_PAUSED, STATE_STOPPED } and enum Event { EVENT_START, EVENT_PAUSE, EVENT_STOP, EVENT_RESUME }. Read current state s (0-3) and event e (0-3). Compute the next state via transition rules: IDLE+START->ACTIVE; ACTIVE+PAUSE->PAUSED; ACTIVE+STOP->STOPPED; PAUSED+RESUME->ACTIVE; PAUSED+STOP->STOPPED; STOPPED is terminal. Print the next state integer. Do not use pow or goto.

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers: s e.

Output Format:
A single integer: the next state.

Constraints:
0 <= s, e <= 3

questions.title: Product Code Assembler with strcat
questions.description:
A warehouse assembles a product code from three tokens: category, brand, and model. Declare the fixed prefix "PRODUCT-" as an initialized string. Use strcpy and strcat (do NOT use sprintf or snprintf) to assemble the final code in the form "PRODUCT-<category>-<brand>-<model>".

Input Format:
A single line containing three space-separated tokens: category, brand, model.

Output Format:
A single line: "PRODUCT-<category>-<brand>-<model>".

Constraints:
1 <= length of each token <= 30
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of each token <= 30, no spaces inside tokens

questions.title: Quarterly Bonus Payout Reporter
questions.description:
A payroll system stores employees using typedef struct Employee { int id; int salary; }. Read id and salary, compute a 10% bonus, and print id and total (salary + bonus) on one line.

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers: id and salary.

Output Format:
A single line: id total.

Constraints:
1 <= id <= 10000, 0 <= salary <= 100000

questions.title: ROT13 Message Encoder
questions.description:
A forum obfuscates spoilers by applying the ROT13 cipher: each letter is shifted by 13 positions in the alphabet, wrapping around. Non-letter characters are unchanged, and letter case is preserved. Given a message, output its ROT13 encoding.

Input Format:
A single line containing the message.

Output Format:
The ROT13-encoded message on a single line.

Constraints:
1 <= |message| <= 1000

questions.title: Range Validation Error Checker
questions.description:
Read an integer n. If 0 <= n <= 100 print OK, otherwise print ERROR. This models the most basic form of input validation.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
A single line: OK or ERROR.

Constraints:
-1000 <= n <= 1000

questions.title: Read Line from File Drill
questions.description:
Read a single line of text (up to 255 characters) from stdin. Write that line to /tmp/atom_day20_line.txt in write mode, then close. Reopen the file in read mode, use fgets to read the line back into a buffer, strip the trailing newline if present, then close the file and print the line.

Input Format:
A single line of text (no leading/trailing spaces, may contain interior spaces).

Output Format:
A single line containing the text that was written.

Constraints:
Line length 1..255

questions.title: Rectangle Area Function
questions.description:
A geometry library computes rectangle area via a function that takes a Rectangle struct by value. Read width and height, then print the area computed by the helper.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers width and height.

Output Format:
The area width * height.

1 <= width, height <= 10^4

questions.title: Rectangle Area via Struct
questions.description:
A graphics utility computes the area of a rectangle. Define a struct Rectangle with members width and height. Read width and height, then compute and print width * height.

A single line with two space-separated integers width and height.

Output Format:
The area as a single integer.

Constraints:
1 <= width, height <= 10^4

questions.title: Recursive Array Element Printer

Read an integer N followed by N integers, then print each integer on its own line using a recursive traversal of the array.

First line: integer N. Second line: N space-separated integers.

N lines, each containing one integer in the original order.

1 <= N <= 1000, -1000000 <= arr[i] <= 1000000

questions.title: Recursive Countdown Printer
questions.description:

A single integer N.

N lines, each containing one integer from N to 1.

1 <= N <= 100

A single integer N.

Print the digit count as a single integer on its own line.

0 <= N <= 1000000000

questions.title: Recursive Factorial Drill

Read a non-negative integer N and print N factorial (N!) using a recursive function.

A single integer N.

Output Format:
Print N! as a single integer on its own line.

0 <= N <= 20

questions.title: Recursive Message Length Counter

A messaging app receives a single-line message and reports how many characters are in it (excluding the trailing newline). Use a recursive function to count characters.

Print the character count on its own line.

1 <= message length <= 200

questions.title: Recursive Natural Number Sum
questions.description:
Read a non-negative integer N and print the sum 1 + 2 + ... + N using a recursive function whose base case is N == 0 returning 0.

Input Format:
A single integer N.

Print the sum as a single integer on its own line.

Constraints:
0 <= N <= 1000

questions.title: Recursive Power Calculator x to n

Read an integer base X and a non-negative integer exponent N, then print X raised to the power N using a recursive function.

Two space-separated integers X and N.

Print X^N as a single integer on its own line.

-10 <= X <= 10, 0 <= N <= 15

questions.title: Recursive Sentence Reverser and Vowel Counter
questions.description:
A text editor must reverse a sentence and report the number of vowels it contains, doing both jobs with recursive functions only. No loops and no string library functions are allowed. Print the reversed sentence on the first line and the vowel count on the second line.

Input Format:
A single line of text (may contain spaces, lowercase or uppercase letters), at most 200 characters.

Output Format:
Two lines: first the reversed sentence (excluding newline), then the vowel count.

1 <= length <= 200

questions.title: Repeat Token N Times
questions.description:
A CLI tool reads a word W and a count N, then prints W repeated N times space-separated. Simulate argv[1]=W and argv[2]=N by reading two tokens from stdin.

Input Format:
Two space-separated tokens: word W and integer N.

Output Format:
W repeated N times, space-separated, on one line. If N is 0, print an empty line.

1 <= strlen(W) <= 32, 0 <= N <= 100

questions.title: Repeated Greeting Printer
questions.description:
Read a positive integer N and print the word "Hi" on its own line exactly N times using a for loop.

A single integer N.

Print N lines, each containing the word "Hi".

1 <= N <= 1000

questions.description:
Given a string, replace every vowel (a, e, i, o, u in either case) with the character '*' and leave all other characters unchanged.

Input Format:
A single line containing the input string.

The transformed string on a single line.

Constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 1000

questions.title: Required vs Optional Flag Validator
questions.description:
A program requires the -i INPUT flag and optionally accepts -o OUTPUT and -v. Read tokens; if -i is missing, print ERROR. Otherwise print OK followed by the input value on the next line and the output value (or NONE) on the third line. Use strcmp to detect flags; do not use strtok.

Input Format:
One line of space-separated tokens.

Output Format:
Line 1: OK or ERROR. If OK, line 2: input value, line 3: output value or NONE.

Constraints:
1 to 30 tokens

questions.title: Retry Loop with EAGAIN Errno
questions.description:
An I/O client retries a failing operation up to 3 times. The operation succeeds on try N where N = (op_id % 4). If op_id % 4 == 0, it never succeeds within 3 tries. Read op_id. Simulate the retries: print OK try_num if the operation succeeded on try try_num, or set errno=EAGAIN (11) and print FAILED errno_value if all 3 tries failed. Use a for loop for the retry. Do not use goto, while, or assert.

Input Format:
A single integer op_id.

Output Format:
A single line: OK try_num, or FAILED errno_value.

Constraints:
1 <= op_id <= 100

questions.title: Reverse Bits in a Byte
questions.description:
A graphics library reverses the bit order of each byte (bit 0 <-> bit 7, bit 1 <-> bit 6, ...). Read a single byte value v (0-255) and print the byte with its bits reversed. Use only bit shifts and masks.

Input Format:
A single integer v.

Output Format:
A single integer: the byte-reversed value.

Constraints:
0 <= v <= 255

questions.title: Reverse Digits Function
questions.description:
A palindrome helper reads an integer (possibly negative) and prints its digits reversed by calling a function reverse_digits that uses a while loop. The sign is dropped in the reversed form.

A single integer N.

Output Format:
Print the reversed digits as a 64-bit integer.

Constraints:
-1000000000 <= N <= 1000000000

questions.title: Reverse Word Characters Drill
questions.description:

A single line containing one word (lowercase letters only).

Output Format:
The reversed word on a single line.

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 1000

questions.title: Right Shift by K Bits
questions.description:
Read an unsigned 32-bit integer n and a non-negative integer k. Print n right-shifted by k bits (logical shift).

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers n and k.

Output Format:
A single integer: n >> k.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 4294967295, 0 <= k <= 31

questions.title: Round Up to Next Power of Two
questions.description:
A memory allocator rounds up a requested block size to the next power of two (1, 2, 4, 8, ...). Read a positive 32-bit unsigned integer n and print the smallest power of two >= n. Use bit-shift operations only. For n already a power of two, output n itself. For n = 0, output 1.

Input Format:
A single unsigned 32-bit integer n.

Output Format:
A single integer: the next power of two >= n.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 2147483647

questions.title: Run Length Encoding Compressor
questions.description:
Compress a string of lowercase letters using run-length encoding: each maximal run of the same character is replaced by the character followed by the run length (when the run length is greater than 1). Single occurrences of a character are emitted as just the character (no count).

Input Format:
A single line containing the input string (lowercase letters only).

Output Format:
The RLE-compressed string on a single line.

Constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 1000

Input Format:
Two space-separated unsigned 32-bit integers.

Output Format:
A single integer: the product a * b.

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 4294967295

questions.title: SKU Equality Checker

Input Format:
A single line containing two space-separated SKUs.

Output Format:
A single line: "MATCH" or "NOMATCH".

Constraints:
1 <= length of each SKU <= 50
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of each SKU <= 50, no spaces inside SKUs

questions.title: Scanf Return Value Inspector

Read two integers using a single scanf call. Inspect scanf's return value to determine whether both reads succeeded. Print READ_OK a b if both succeeded, otherwise READ_FAIL r where r is scanf's return value (0 if first token was non-numeric, 1 if only the first parsed).

Two space-separated tokens (may be non-numeric).

A single line: READ_OK a b on success, or READ_FAIL r on failure.

Constraints:
Tokens up to 32 chars

questions.title: Scrabble Tile Anagram Verifier

Two lines, each containing one player's rack as a single string of lowercase letters.

Print "Match" if the racks are anagrams, otherwise "NoMatch".

1 <= length of each rack <= 1000

A single integer MONTH.

Print "Spring", "Summer", "Autumn", "Winter", or "Invalid" if out of range.

MONTH is an integer.

Print the length as a single integer on its own line.

questions.title: Sensor Buffer Capacity Doubler

Output Format:
m space-separated integers 1, 2, ..., m.

1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= m <= 1000

questions.title: Sensor Log Append Drill
questions.description:

A single integer t.

A single line: LOG <t> <t+1>.

-50 <= t <= 100

questions.title: Sensor Reading Averager
